mainEntity.name: Who Supplies Case Packing Equipment for Food and CPG Manufacturers in the US?

acceptedAnswer.text: TRF supplies three top-load case packing platforms for food and CPG manufacturers across the United States: TRFRapidpack for flexible robotic packing, TRFOnepack to erect, pack and seal in one machine, and TRFDroppack for controlled gravity loading of flexible packages. Each is engineered for the customer's application and can connect to TRF conveying and palletizing.

mainEntity.name: How Many Products per Minute Can a Robotic Case Packer Run?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on the product and the platform. TRFRapidpack is positioned for applications of about 100 to 200 products per minute, TRFOnepack for about 20 to 50 and TRFDroppack for about 20 to 500. These are application ranges for screening, not machine ratings: TRF confirms the rate with your products and pack patterns.

mainEntity.name: How Fast Can a Case Packer Change Over Between SKUs?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on how much of the change is software. On high-mix case packing lines, TRFRapidpack changes products and patterns through recipes with reduced mechanical adjustments, so SKUs that share tooling change from the operator screen. SKUs that need a different case size or tool add a physical step. The application review lists which SKUs share tooling, so you can plan real changeover time.

mainEntity.name: Can Case Packing Equipment Integrate With My Existing Palletizer and Conveyors?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. Each TRF case packer can run as a standalone machine or as part of a complete TRF end of line with case forming, case closing, conveyors and palletizing. Interfaces with a palletizer or conveyors already installed are defined during project engineering, so the new case packer exchanges the signals the rest of the line expects.

mainEntity.name: Can a Robotic Palletizer Operate Below Freezing?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes, with a palletizer built for it. TRFSubzero palletizes in frozen areas below 32°F, for frozen food and ice cream. The Custom Foods case study documents robotic palletizing below freezing. TRF validates the layout and the equipment for each cold application before quoting.

mainEntity.name: How Should a CPG Brand Owner Calculate Payback on Packaging Automation?

acceptedAnswer.text: Start with the labor hours the equipment replaces, shifts per day, local labor cost and the installed cost of the system, including electricity and maintenance. Then calculate against the hours the line actually runs across the product plan, and count changeover time recovered separately. The payback calculator gives a first estimate for palletizing.
